question: GQ-001
subject: three passes to find every non-book in one want-list

the_sequence.failures: 77 NO_TEXT, zero letters — property photographs by street address
36 NO_TEXT — court filings and photographs named by STYLE, not address

why_it_took_three: each rule removed one shape and revealed the next. The Architecture subject pulled in an entire photographic survey of La Canada Flintridge plus a 52-part court docket, and no single pattern describes all of it.

the_new_rules.court_filing: requires BOTH a "v." case name AND an explicit (Part N of M), so "Part 2 of the Gardener's Kalendar" cannot match
the_new_rules.photo_view_note: a parenthetical view-note — (front view), (interior detail) — which a catalogue adds to a photograph and never to a book

false_positive_checks.photo_pattern_across_the_whole_list: 17 matches, every one a California home from the same survey

the_structural_payoff: all four rules sit behind one isNotABook predicate imported by both builders, so each addition reached the want-list AND the index builder at once — the thing that had to be fixed by hand when the correspondence rule was added alone.
